Before/After detection uses text_lower.find('\n#### before') and '\n#### after' which will miss headings at the start of the file or headings without a preceding newline and is brittle to whitespace/capitalization; use a Markdown-aware regex or normalize line starts when searching headings.

parse_agents_blocks uses ln.startswith('## ') to detect agent headers; this is brittle because headings with leading spaces will be missed — use ln.lstrip().startswith('## ') or a regex to robustly detect Markdown headings.

The consolidated validator repeats the same brittle checks (Before/After detection and header detection) from earlier cells; hard-coded string searches and simplistic code-fence counting can produce false negatives/positives — recommend normalizing lines, using regex for headings, and verifying code-fence pairing instead of raw counts.

The notebook's runner code looks for a single-line JSON object by checking lines that start with '{' and end with '}' which will fail if the script emits pretty-printed/multi-line JSON; either ensure the validator prints compact JSON or parse stdout until a valid JSON object is found (or capture stdout as one string and json.loads()).
